points.text: This page lists events in the UK and Ireland. They have a BSL or ISL interpreter.
Type a name or place to search. You can pick a type of event, like concerts or sport.
You can pick a place. You can also pick a date.
Pick Sports to see football clubs and their matches.
Booked means an interpreter is booked. On request means you can ask for one.
BSL means British Sign Language. ISL means Irish Sign Language.
We write an email to the venue for you. A venue is the place of the event.
First, tell us about the event you want to go to.
We fill in the venue's email if we have it. If not, you can type one in.
You can change the words in the email. Then send it. We get a copy.
We will help if you need us.

signed.label: How to ask for an interpreter

points.text: This page has contacts for venues in the UK and Ireland. A venue is the place of an event.
Search for a venue by name. You can also pick a country, then a city.
Can't find your venue? We can help you write an email to the venue.
You can also contact us. We reply within 48 hours.

No interpreter at an event? The app writes the message to ask for one.

We bring interpreters to live events in the UK and Ireland. BSL is British Sign Language and ISL is Irish Sign Language.
Marie Pascall started Performance Interpreting. She was born deaf in one ear.
We have worked at more than 600 events. We started more than 10 years ago.
Every interpreter is on the NRCPD register. NRCPD is the UK register for people who work with Deaf people.
We gave evidence in the Little Mix BSL court case. It helped show that the law says live events need BSL.
Wembley Stadium promised BSL interpreting at every concert. We worked with them on this.
We give event organisers BSL interpreters and advice. BSL means British Sign Language.
First, tell us about your event. Then we plan the access and prepare the interpreters.
Book as soon as you know your dates. We will tell you honestly if a request is too late.
The Equality Act 2010 is a law. It says you must make reasonable changes for Deaf customers.
Your event appears in the PI Events App when you book with us. The app is free to download.
Every interpreter is on the NRCPD register. NRCPD is the UK register for sign language interpreters.
We work with interpreters at festivals, arenas and Premier League clubs. BSL means British Sign Language and ISL means Irish Sign Language.
You must have current NRCPD registration. NRCPD is the register for sign language interpreters.
Live events experience helps but is not always needed. We also look for people who stay calm and work well in a team.
The PI Academy is our training team. It offers courses and mentoring for interpreters.
You can volunteer with us to see how live events run. Deaf volunteers fluent in BSL can join. Others need BSL Level 6 or above.
To join, send us a message. Tell us about your NRCPD registration and the events you have worked at.
We provide BSL interpreters at big music festivals, like Reading, Leeds and Download. BSL means British Sign Language.
Use the free PI Events App to find acts with BSL or ISL. It shows the stage, the time and the interpreter.
You can see interpreter names and profiles before you go. You can ask for BSL or ISL at sets that do not have it.
After the festival, tell us how access went. You can write to us or send a sign language video.
We also work at Irish festivals, like Electric Picnic. ISL means Irish Sign Language.
Festival organisers can ask us to plan access and manage the interpreter team.

signed.label: What to do at the event

points.text: We provide BSL interpreters at Premier League matches and big sports events. BSL means British Sign Language.
We work with clubs like Arsenal, Chelsea, Fulham and West Ham. We are also the Deaf access provider for Wembley Stadium.
We interpret announcements, half-time shows and interviews. We also cover FA Cup finals and EFL Cup finals.
Use the free PI Events App to find matches with BSL. You can also ask for BSL at a match that does not have it.
After the match, tell us how access went. You can write to us or send a sign language video.
Clubs can book us for matches across the whole season.

signed.label: Your rights as a Deaf customer

points.text: This page explains how we look after your data. Your data means information about you.
We collect your name, email and phone number when you contact us. We also keep details about events and bookings.
Our website counts page visits without cookies.
We do not sell your data. We share it only when we need to, like telling interpreters about your event.
You can ask to see your data. You can ask us to fix it or delete it.
To use your rights, email admin@performanceinterpreting.co.uk. We reply within 1 month.
This page explains how the PI Events app treats your information.
The app can use your microphone. The sound stays on your phone and is never recorded.
The Near Me filter is optional. Your location stays on your phone. We never get it.
You can send us a feedback video in BSL or ISL. Only people in our team can watch it.
We do not sell your data. We do not track you for adverts.
You can ask us to delete your data. Email admin@performanceinterpreting.co.uk.
